en: Salutations to the illustrious Śrīnivāsa.
Here begins the fifth question in the *Śrīvaikhānasamantrapraśnāṣṭaka*.
5.1.1.1 Hariḥ Oṃ! May the Blessed Lord Viṣṇu, Hari, the sovereign of all gods,
who bears the Śrīvatsa mark, possesses a thousand eyes, and likewise a thousand feet, be pleased.
5.1.1.2 O lotus-eyed one, homage to you! O creator of the universe, homage to you! Homage be to you, O Hṛṣīkeśa, Great Being, Primordial One.
5.1.1.3 May all the signs known as auspicious be endowed with beauty.
"O Viṣṇu, by your grace we have come together as your servants;
let us prepare your celestial chariot, may you show us favor,
and let all your attendants provide assistance at your command."
5.1.1.5 Let us indeed send forth the peaceful, pervasive beings and so forth;
having repeatedly severed obstacles, let him who does not fall away proceed ahead. *Note on grammar:* This is an irregular *bahuvrīhi* compound accentuation. Cf. *A Vedic Grammar for Students*.
A.A. MacDonell, p. 455a.
[*2] Syllables that are underlined receive a "double svarita," indicated by two parallel vertical lines above the syllable.
In the published text. [*3] Cf. Kāśyapa Jñāna Kāṇḍaḥ, chapter 34.
If the *vīśa* is deficient, there will be an increase of enemies.
Let Nandaka proceed at the back; let the mace protect the left side well;
and let the conch and the spear strive on the other two sides for the accomplishment of the task.
5.1.2.2 "By your grace, may all the remaining [tasks] proceed with us in every way.
O hero, through your favor, we shall build your house. 5.1.2.3 "Just as the sun, having assumed heat, burns even a stone, so shall it be for you."
Likewise, by your power, may we indeed maintain our service;
if you have compassion for us, who are your servants, please grant your consent. We all entreat you with joy.
5.1.2.5 May the Lord Viṣṇu, Indra of a hundred powers, the hero, the king of all, the husband of Śacī, the bestower of auspiciousness upon all the worlds, be pleased.
[*4] The published text provides the following variant, which I have translated into English:
Just as a stone is heated by the sun, though it is not inherently hot, yet it assumes heat;
so too may the foremost of purifiers, Agni; the leader of the gods, Hari;
the Blessed Lord Viṣṇu, the enjoyer of all and the bringer of happiness, be pleased. 5.1.3.1

5.1.3.2 Viṣṇu is the source of all worlds; he is Yama, the executor of justice, who is dear to his subjects, the wielder of the rod of punishment, the leader, the soul of righteousness, and the protector of dharma.
5.1.3.3 Protecting his subjects and slaying the Yātudhānas, he is indeed the unborn Lord.
May Nirṛti be pleased; may Nīla, who has the luster of the petals of a blue lotus, be pleased.
May the Lord Varuṇa, the wise and powerful protector of sacrifice, the hero clad in red garments, the imperishable Master, be pleased.

5.1.3.5 May the auspicious Vāyu, the soul of all, the swift Udāna, Marut, and the Lord Prāṇa, the friend of Śacī’s husband and the Sovereign, be pleased. 5.1.3.6 [May] Kubera, the king of kings, the lord of wealth, and the son of Viśravas [be pleased].
May the Lord, the friend of Īśvara, who is endowed with treasures, be pleased.
May the three-eyed Lord, the wielder of the trident, whose banner and vehicle is the bull, the eternal sustainer of the Gaṇas, Tryambaka, who resembles the sky, be pleased. 5.1.3.7
5.1.3.8 May Brahmā, the Grandfather, the Hero, the speaker of the Vedas, Vṛṣākapi,
who resembles the interior of a lotus, the son of Viṣṇu, the Virāṭ, and the Svarāṭ, be pleased.
5.1.3.9 May the elephants of the quarters, the hosts of serpents, and all the intermediate deities [be pleased].

May the planets beginning with the Sun, the spirits, the seers, the *siddhas* and *cāraṇas*, together with their hosts, grant favor and provide assistance. [Daḷa 5.1.0.1] Furthermore, may the Lord, who repeatedly bestows auspiciousness, [be present]. And nine...
5.1.4.1 To Rudra, to Bhūta, to Indra, to Yama, to Soma, to Vīra, to Rudra, to Indra, to Yama, and to the lords of the trees; 5.1.4.2 homage to the lords of the forest; 5.1.4.3 homage to the maidens.
5.1.4.4 Homage to the kings of trees!
5.1.4.5 Homage to those who grant all desires!
5.1.4.6 Svāhā to Agni!
5.1.4.7 Svāhā to the king of the forest! 5.1.4.8 Svāhā to Soma!
5.1.5.1 Svāhā to Yama!
5.1.5.2 Svāhā to the branch!
5.1.5.3 Svāhā to the thick lac!
5.1.5.4 Svāhā to the hunter!

5.1.8.2 Svāhā to the twilight deities!

5.1.8.10 Svāhā to the forest!
5.1.8.11 Svāhā to the land-dweller!
5.1.8.12 Svāhā to the tree deities! 5.1.8.13 Svāhā to the place deities!
5.1.8.14 Svāhā to the Vidyādharas!
5.1.8.15 Svāhā to the embodied ones!
5.1.8.16 Svāhā to the pairs!
5.1.8.17 Svāhā to pleasures! 5.1.8.18 Bhūḥ svāhā!
5.1.0.2 Svāhā to Soma! Svāhā to Śalātu! Svāhā to the three-handed one! Svāhā to those who roam by day! Svāhā to the forest! And eight [oblations].
5.1.9.1 The Rākṣasa is burnt away. 5.1.9.2 To the Lord of All, Svāhā!
5.1.9.3 To the Master of the World, Svāhā!
5.1.9.4 Svāhā to Cāmuṇḍā!
5.1.9.5 Svāhā to Sarvataścarā! 5.1.9.6 Svāhā to Brahmāṇī!
5.1.9.7 Svāhā to Piṅgalā! 5.1.9.8 Svāhā to Gaurī! 5.1.9.9 Svāhā to Sarvatomukhī!
5.1.9.10 Svāhā to Saritpriyā. [6] To Piṅgalā. 5.1.10.1 Svāhā to Viśvarūpā.
5.1.10.2 Svāhā to Ugrā! 5.1.10.3 Svāhā to Gaṇeśvarī! 5.1.10.4 Svāhā to Vaiśākhinī!
5.1.10.5 Svāhā to Śikhaṇḍinī!
5.1.10.6 Svāhā to Gāyatrī! 5.1.10.7 Svāhā to Ṣaṇmukhī!
5.1.10.8 Svāhā to Viśvagarbhā! 5.1.10.9 Svāhā to Viṣormiṇī! 5.1.10.10 Svāhā to Kṛṣṇā!
5.1.11.1 Svāhā to Druhiṇī! 5.1.11.2 Svāhā to Vārāhī!
5.1.11.3 Svāhā to Varadā!
5.1.11.4 Svāhā to Urvī!
5.1.11.5 Svāhā to Vajradaṃṣṭrī! 5.1.11.6 Svāhā to Jayantī!
5.1.11.7 Svāhā to Kauśikī! 5.1.11.8 Svāhā to Indrāṇī! 5.1.11.9 Svāhā to Ghanāghananī!
5.1.11.10 Svāhā to Kālyā! 5.1.11.11 Svāhā to Nālīkadaṃṣṭrī! 5.1.11.12 Svāhā to Vṛṣabhā!
5.1.11.13 Svāhā to Veda-dhāriṇī (the bearer of the Vedas).
5.1.11.14 Svāhā to Vakratuṇḍa (the one with the curved trunk). 5.1.11.15 Svāhā to Eka-daṃṣṭra (the one with the single tusk).
5.1.11.16 Svāhā to Vikaṭa!
5.1.11.17 Svāhā to Vināyaka!
5.1.11.18 Bhūḥ! Svāhā!

5.1.12.1 These animals are pure. 5.1.12.2 At the seven streams. 5.1.12.3 May they measure out well-being for us.
Bestower of well-being, Lord of the people;
[Salutation] to Nārāyaṇa.
Oṃ, I invoke Śeṣa.
5.1.12.6 I invoke Medinī.
5.1.12.7 I invoke Jyeṣṭhā. 5.1.12.8 I invoke Vāyu.
5.1.12.9 I invoke Indra.
5.1.12.10 I invoke the Maruts.

5.1.13.1 I invoke the Lord of Waters; I invoke Yama; [I invoke] King Soma—I invoke Soma.
5.1.13.2 All-conquering, slayer of all enemies, unfailing, possessed of incomparable heroism.
May the Blessed One, the wheel-turner who brings about the dissolution of all things, come!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvas suvas subhū svayambhū!
Vainateya, of great heroism, the son of Kaśyapa, whose radiance is like fire!
May the Blessed King come, the conqueror of serpents, whose vehicle is Viṣṇu. 5.1.13.5 Let there be a seat...
5.1.13.6 Welcome to the king of birds, the consumer of serpents, the architect of the universe.
To the most excellent among those born from eggs, equal in splendor to Viṣṇu— be well-pleased as the one who authorizes the ritual act of your husband;
may this imperishable one himself accept all this with his permissions.
5.1.13.9 “For you, O waters, are indeed sources of bliss” (RV 10.9.1); “That [glory] of Savitṛ” (RV 3.62.10).
5.1.13.10 May the Lord of Thought make thee lustrous; may we be possessed of splendor.
5.1.13.11 May the Lord of Prosperity bestow prosperity here; may he cause progeny to delight here.
To Prajāpati, lord of nourishment, lord of fire, lord of wealth, [and] to Desire for the sake of food—[one offers] King Soma as the *pratīka*:

5.1.14.1 May the divine Lord come— self-controlled, peaceful, beloved by the people,
the most excellent among all devotees, the giver of wealth at all times, the bestower of boons.
5.1.14.2 [He who dwells] in the seven streams.
5.1.14.3 Therefore, O gods, [sing] aloud at his birth.
5.1.14.4 May the beloved goddess Medinī be pleased; for this is the determination of the site for that horn by which she was uplifted—the wife of a hero, large-eyed.
"O fair-faced one, having reached that [place] without any obstacle, may we accomplish this;
[homage to] the goddess Medinī,
[and] homage to Varuṇa."
5.1.14.7 Do not gamble with dice; practice agriculture instead; take delight in your wealth, considering it abundant.
[Note: The 1946 published edition provides the variant reading *śānto dānto*.
Compare the unusual accentuation here with 5.1.1.1.]
May the Blessed Viṣṇu be pleased.
Here *priyatām* has only one accent. RV 10.34.13ab.
5.1.15.1 There are cows there, O gambler; there is a wife there. This the noble Savitṛ has revealed to me.

5.1.15.2 You are the bull, you are the ancient one, you indeed are the primordial one, you are the knower of the Vedas, you are the four-horned one. 5.1.15.3 Manu himself has said this to you: "I shall yoke you. O hero, bear the yoke for the sake of the gods; you are a hero."
5.1.15.4 O descendant of Śūra, vehicle of the Lord of the Gods, portion of Viṣṇu, friend of Viṣṇu, Lord of the cows!
5.1.15.5 Plow this earth for the sake of a dwelling for Viṣṇu.
5.1.15.6 I yoke the pair with horns like the cosmic age (yuga) for the purpose of yoga.
5.1.15.7 I seize the seer for the sake of extraction, by the command of the sages.
5.1.15.8 May Viṣṇu protect me.
5.1.15.9 Those living beings who live in this region, [may they be] protected.
O you who have become *piśācinīs* joined with other deities, listen!
This place of the Lord of All has been prepared for your dwelling.
Depart from here as you please; may there be another delightful [place] for you. May it be well with you; may there be prosperity.

5.1.15.11 May those ploughed by the plow go to heaven; may those crushed [by it] go to the world of Vāyu. May those afflicted by exhaustion attain immortality. 5.1.15.12 And may he duly extract their vigor.
5.1.15.13 May the Sun be dear to the eyes of all.
"O Daityas, let only auspicious deeds be performed; the Blessed One, the Enemy of the Daityas, is here.

The phrase "the published text" refers to both the 1946 and 1984 editions. 5.1.0.5 Thinking it to be conducive to cultivation, [he offered] seven [seeds]. 5.1.16.1 These seeds—rice and barley—may they sprout by the grace of the sun's rays.
May those offered with Soma and seized by the planets become free from disease, pure, and auspicious.
(5.1.16.2) I sow upon the earth the sprouting seeds, seventeen in number, which were created by Brahmā. May they all, nourished by the power of rain and protected by nectar, sustain the worlds.
(5.1.16.3) May those seven domestic and seven wild plants—which have perished in the heat or been produced by frost and rain—having become rain itself, protect us with nectar.

5.1.16.4 May those that are split, moist, dried, and growing—abounding in roots, fruits, and vegetables of excellent form—grow like grass for the sake of cattle: as food for mortals and as sacrificial oblation (*havis*) for the gods.
5.1.16.5 For the purification of the earth and for the sake of establishing the order of the gods, I sow these seeds.

5.1.16.6. Those seeds that grow as the products of the conjunction of ether, earth, fire, water, and air—I offer them all as seeds for purification in the divine rite, for the sake of establishing the divine order. [*31] The 1946 text reads *martyānṃ*. The 1984 text reads *martyān*, assuming that what appears to be a second *r* is actually a symbol for final *n* with one loop broken off. Otherwise, as it stands, [the reading remains as it is].

The 1984 edition reads *martyā*. I have corrected all these unintelligible forms to *martyānām*, which, when combined with *annena*, yields an intelligible reading parallel to *haviṣā surāṇām* [*32*].
The text places an *anudātta* beneath the *ū* of *bhūmy* and then a *svarita* above the *a* of *agni*.

5.1.17.1 May the winds carry that which is the seed of this intermediate space, and that which is the seed— fire, earth, and moisture— for the sake of the growth of seeds.
May they grow and flourish;
may those many shoots grow free from harm. For seeds sown are made to sprout by time and the wind of immortality as they are nurtured; from the seed I shall spread the Dharma.

5.1.17.3 May these seeds, having become sap, flow forth, created by Soma and like nectar for the cattle. Having eaten these sprouts born from the essence of sap which have been given to me, may the cows thrive.
5.1.17.4 Therefore, I sow these in your house; may they carry my cattle as nectar.

May these [seeds], praised by me, flow forth for me in that world of merit hereafter, having become my very body. 5.1.17.5 On every peak of the Ocean-clad mountain, 5.1.17.6 O Goddess, I sow these [seeds] in you; perform [this task].
I milk you, the wish-fulfilling cow, for the abundance of grain; O wish-fulfilling cow with grain as your calf, fill me with heaps of wealth.
May Indra milk the heavens.

"‘O Agni, you are great,’ he says, for this Agni is indeed great. ‘O Brāhmaṇa,’ he says, for he is indeed a Brāhmaṇa. ‘O Bhārata...’"
"He brings the oblation to the gods," he says, for he is kindled by the gods; "kindled by the gods," he says, for the gods indeed kindle him;
"kindled by Manu," he says, for Manu indeed kindled him after the gods; "praised by the seers," he says, for the seers indeed praised him;
"rejoiced in by the sages," he says. (1)

"For these are indeed the Brahmins who have heard [the Vedas]," he says; for he is one whose intellect is sharpened by the Veda (*brahma-saṃśita*). "He is one who offers oblations of clarified butter," he says; for the offering of clarified butter is his most beloved. "The leader of sacrifices," he says; for he is the leader of sacrifices.
"The charioteer of rituals," he says; for he is the divine chariot of the gods. "The invincible Hotṛ-priest," he says; for no one at all [can overcome him]. (2)
"He crosses swiftly, the bearer of oblations," he says, for he indeed crosses everything. "The ladle of the gods," he says, for he is indeed the ladle of the gods.

"The cup for the drinking of the gods," he says, for he is indeed the cup for the drinking of the gods. "Like the felly, O Agni, thou encompassest the gods," he says, for he indeed encompasses the gods. [If he were to say,] "Bring hither the gods..."
‘For the sacrificer who seeks the gods’—[if he were to say this,] he would produce a rival for him.
‘Bring the gods hither for the sacrificer,’ he says; by this, he causes the sacrificer himself to prosper. ...
Keith’s translation: “‘O Agni, ...”
"Thou art great," he says, for Agni is great. "O Brahman," he says...
He says this,
for he is a Brahmin; "O Bhārata," he says.
For he carries the sacrifice to the gods. "Enkindled by the gods," he says, for the gods enkindled him; "enkindled by Manu," [he says].
He says this,
for Manu enkindled him after the gods. "Praised by the ṛṣis," he says.
For the ṛṣis praised him; "delighted by sages," he says, for learned men are sages; "celebrated by poets."
He says this because the learned are the poets. "Impelled by Brahman," he says, for he is indeed impelled by Brahman.
"With an oblation of clarified butter," he says, for clarified butter is his most beloved oblation. "The leader of the sacrifices."
He says this,
for he is the leader of the sacrifices. "The charioteer of the rites," he says.
For he is the chariot of the gods. "The Hotṛ who is unsurpassed," he says, for no one surpasses him. "Surpassing..."
"Bearing the oblation," he says,
for he surpasses all. "The mouth-dish..."
"The ladle of the gods," he says,
for he is indeed the ladle of the gods; "the bowl from which the gods drink."
So he says,
for he is the bowl from which the gods drink: "O Agni,
as the spokes [are fixed] in the rim..."
‘Thou encompassest the gods,’ he says, for he indeed encompasses the gods. If he were to say—

“If he were to say, ‘Bring the gods hither to the pious sacrificer,’ he would create an enemy for him. He says, ‘Bring the gods hither to the sacrificer’; verily, by this he causes the sacrificer to grow great.”

Homage to the fatness (*medas*). Come now, O Indra! May Viṣṇu protect me. Homage to the blood, homage to the skin. Homage to Life, homage to Brahman.

To you, the newly born teacher, O Lord of the Dwelling (*vāstoṣ-pati*), [I offer] for the sake of the crest-garland, *svāhā*; for the pinnacle (*sthūpikā*), *svāhā*. These are pure; you are the bright one. I praise Agni; I invoke the *gārhapatya* sacrifice. For food (*iṣ*) you, for strength (*ūrj*) you. Water indeed is all this. The Self is subtler than an atom. Therefore, O Gods... This is Viṣṇu. *Oṃ*. May the Blessed One come; I invoke the *Atharva-veda*.

The beginning of the sixth inquiry.
6.1.1 Hariḥ Oṃ.
6.1.2 May the gods protect us from that place whence Viṣṇu strode forth.
With the seven abodes of the earth, svāhā! 6.1.3 Viṣṇu strode across this; he established his foot in three places; his [foot] is gathered together. (pāda)
To the Lord, svāhā!
6.1.4 Viṣṇu, the undeceivable guardian, strode forth his three steps; from there he established the laws of righteousness, svāhā!
6.1.5 Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made his vows manifest—he who is the inseparable friend of Indra. Svāhā!
6.1.6 That is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
The wise always behold him, like an eye extended across the sky; svāhā!
6.1.7 The inspired poets, ever-watchful and praising, kindle him together.
That which is the supreme station of Viṣṇu, svāhā! [327] RV: From here, the eye is extended.
ṃ svāhā. And two [more]:
6.2.1[*328] The Puruṣa has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet.
Having pervaded the earth on all sides, he stood beyond it by ten fingers' breadth. Svāhā!
6.2.2 This entire world is indeed the Person—whatever has been and whatever is to be; moreover, he is the Lord of immortality, that which grows by means of food. Svāhā!
6.2.3 Such is his greatness, and the Puruṣa is even greater than this.
All beings constitute one quarter of him; his three quarters are the immortal in heaven. Svāhā!
6.2.4 With three quarters the Puruṣa rose upward; one quarter of him remained here again. From there he strode out in all directions toward what is eaten and what is not eaten. Svāhā!
6.2.5 From him Virāj was born; from Virāj the Puruṣa was born.
Once born, he extended beyond the earth behind and also before; svāhā!
6.3.1 When the gods performed the sacrifice with man as the oblation, spring was its clarified butter, summer the fuel, and autumn the oblation—svāhā!
6.3.2 Seven were its enclosing sticks; thrice seven were the fuel-sticks prepared.
When the gods, performing the sacrifice, bound Puruṣa as the victim, svāhā!
6.3.3 They sprinkled that sacrifice upon the sacrificial grass—Puruṣa who was born in the beginning; with him the gods, the Sādhyas, and the Ṛṣis sacrificed, svāhā!
6.3.4 From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, he gathered the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya) and made those animals— the ones belonging to Vāyu, whether wild or domestic— his own; svāhā!
6.3.5 From that sacrifice, from which all was offered, the *ṛc* verses and the *sāman* chants were born;
the meters were born from it, and from it the *yajus* formula was produced. *Svāhā!* (RV 10.90.15 [out of order]; TA; VC p. 973)
[*331] From the sacrifice [*332] from the sacrifice [*333] from the all-oblation.
6.4.1 From him were born horses, and whatever animals have two rows of teeth;
from him cows were born, and from him goats and sheep were born. Svāhā!
6.4.2 When they divided the Puruṣa, into how many parts did they apportion him?
"What was its mouth? What were its arms? What are its thighs called, and what its feet? "Svāhā! "The Brāhmaṇa was its mouth; the Rājanya was made its arms;
that which was its thighs was the Vaiśya; from its feet [came the Śūdra]."
From his feet the Śūdra was born, Svāhā!
The moon was born from his mind; from his eye the sun was born;
from his mouth Indra and Agni were born; from his breath Vāyu was born, Svāhā!
From his navel the intermediate space arose; from his head the sky evolved;
from his feet the earth, and from his ears the quarters. Thus they fashioned the worlds. Svāhā!
6.4.6 I know this great Puruṣa, resplendent as the sun, beyond the darkness.
Having surveyed all forms and created names, the Wise One remains uttering them—*svāhā*. 6.4.7 Dhātṛ proclaimed him in the east; Śakra, the wise one, [proclaimed him] in the four quarters.
One who knows this thus becomes immortal here; no other path for going exists. Svāhā!
By means of sacrifice the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice; those were the first ordinances.
Those great ones attained the height of heaven, where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide. Svāhā!

O Jātavedas, bring to me the golden Lakṣmī who is radiant; svāhā!

6.26.1 Let us press the Soma for Jātavedas; may he burn away the wealth of the one who acts with hostility. [*410] *vedaḥ* (wealth).
May he carry us across all difficulties, as one crosses a river with a boat; may Agni carry us beyond misfortunes—*svāhā*.

6.26.2. That goddess Durgā, who is fire-colored, blazing with ascetic heat, the daughter of Virocana, who is gratified by the fruits of ritual action—*tām agni-varṇāṃ tapasā jvalantīṃ vairocanīṃ karma-phaleṣu juṣṭām durgāṃ devīm*.
I go for refuge to you; O Sūtara, you who cross over, obeisance to you, svāhā!

6.26.3 O Agni, as a new one, do you carry us across all difficulties with blessings; may you be a broad, vast, and spacious fortress for us. Be a source of peace and well-being for our children and descendants, svāhā!

6.26.4 O Jātavedas, you who overcome all difficulties, carry us across all misfortunes as one crosses the ocean by boat. O Agni, being praised with a mind like that of Atri, be the protector of our bodies; Svāhā! 6.26.5 Conqueror of hostile armies.
Let us invoke the fierce Agni who endures all; from his highest dwelling place, may he, the god, carry us across all difficulties and beyond all misfortunes— Agni, Svāhā!
6.26.6 You are the ancient one, worthy of praise at the sacrifices; as the Hotṛ-priest from of old, you are both new and ancient.
O Agni, take pleasure in your own body and win for us prosperity through sacrifice. Svāhā!

6.0.8 Svāhā to the sixty-fold one! May these two, dwelling together in the same abode, rejoice; and may the three [beings] likewise rejoice. 6.27.1 May there be a well-offered oblation for Nandinī, Mūlavatī, Jagatī, Vasatī, and Jyeṣṭhā.
Svāhā to the divine Svasṛ (Sister), the Earth, who is fond of silver!
6.27.2 The waters entered with progeny; the wife of Brahmā is the preeminent offspring of Skanda. We know this from the support of the Goddess.
May the swift Goddess grant us protection always. Svāhā!
6.27.3 With a beautiful branch, he joined [it] as a branch to pierce the sky.
Let us worship the Goddess Dhātṛ with the foremost oblations; may she arise there upon the flowing river, Svāhā!
(6.27.4) The Goddess Pravāhinī constantly protects all beings, scattering every meter [of the Veda].
May Jayā bestow auspiciousness upon me who worships her; may she cause my chronic ailment to decay. Svāhā!
6.27.5 Having become a lotus fiber, she releases [the breath] like a mother; moreover, when not yet released, she dwells within the sacred word (brahman).
May I know her through lightning.

I thoroughly satiate [thee], svāhā! 6.28.1. For her who is accompanied by lightning and possesses a well-disposed mind, this path has become one that leads to the far shore; I offer oblations that delight the fingers of the drops; may she, bestowing auspiciousness, be subject to our will, svāhā!
May the speech of Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, bear fruit for our welfare;
may she, ever granting fearlessness, be auspicious. From her I take up the entire essence; may that which is released here by the Goddess into the fire always protect us—svāhā!
May the Mother extend knowledge to us;
may the Soma-like ones cause us to descend into the gentle state.
Through that, may we enter what is revealed limb by limb; may we know this unfailing Brahman through progeny. Svāhā!
6.28.4 For the immeasurable Earth is the Mother in embodied form, by whom one expands one's being among the senses;
she, who was born under the sway of this [Earth], may she, the self-willed one, be for my prosperity—svāhā!
6.28.5 May the wise living beings call upon you, the Mother, so that they may attain the state of discernment and abide in the application of my intellect.
O Pravāhinī, you have carried away my beloved;
do not harm her, svāhā!

Being is the seer’s truth; being is truth. For the path of being, svāhā!
7.2.9.2 [5.2] Truth is light; being is the vital breaths; being is the support; being is the connection.
Truth is being, the manifestation, the light. For light, svāhā!

7.2.10.1 [5.6] That is *bhūḥ*; it is situated in the earth, or it is the one staying on the earth, the universal form. That is *bhūḥ*, reckoned as the vital breath (*prāṇa*). *Bhūr* was; you are *bhūḥ*, you are *bhuvaḥ*, you are *suvar*. *Bhūr* for the sake of prosperity, *svāhā*!
7.2.10.2 [5.7] Water indeed is water; water is the inner self. That which is the Veda is the support of the Vedas.
The inner self of the Vedas, possessing flavor, reckoned as the essence, he who has entered into every flavor—for the sake of that flavor, Svāhā!

7.2.10.3 [5.8] Or rather, the Triple Veda (Trayī) is desire, consisting of the Triple Veda, having three qualities, and characterized by the threefold state; or the Triple Veda is light, having three qualities and consisting of the three qualities—to that Triple Fire, which possesses the three qualities, Svāhā!
7.2.10.4 [5.9] Or, the two principal ones, supported by the principal, together with pleasure, together with bliss, together with smiles, and with long smiles, rejoice with bliss— *svāhā*.
7.2.10.5 [5.10] He is each one individually, having a common support, having a supreme foundation, and having the *in* as his foundation.

To him who bestows a hundredfold, the praiseworthy one, svāhā!

7.2.15.1 [8.1] To that Lord of Gods (Sureśa), who, being subtle, supports the entire universe—which is composed of essence, which is experienced for the most part as joy, and which is permeated by him—to that Lord of Gods, svāhā to this entirely meritorious offering.

7.2.15.2 [8.2] This is indeed the fruit of the worlds, the undecaying Great Soul who protects the universe, stainless and named the Immaculate. To him, the giver of boons, for his protection and nourishment, Svāhā! 7.2.15.3 [8.3] May they bear our burden, delighting in joy; may those possessing manly prosperity be well-disposed toward us at the appointed time. Svāhā!
Aṃ! To the one possessing streaks, for the protection of the whole, svāhā!
7.2.15.4 [8.4] You bear the entire universe, including the gods and the weeping ones—the one possessing complete streaks, fully grown.
May he, having spread himself out, cast us into the vessel; *svāhā*!

7.2.15.5 [8.5] Or rather, he who is of his own nature, all-seeing and complete, piercing the moon, or who, bestowing his footstep in the sky, shines with great growth—him, the possessed of the orb, the all-joyous and complete one, *svāhā*.
7.2.16.1 [8.6] Whether it be *bhūḥ*, *bhuvaḥ*, *bhuvaḥ*, or *suvaḥ*—whatever resounds, all that has been brought forth by Him;
the Giver of all, the undecaying, [He grants] His own [bliss] to the singer.
7.2.16.2 [8.7] Having withdrawn the entire expansion that had spread out within Dākṣāyaṇī, [He remains as] the whole.
May he, dwelling with me, grant all that is most excellent; to that Lord of Creatures, the bearer of the burden, Svāhā!

7.2.16.3 [8.8] May he, crossing over all hopes within, dwell in those various forms which are entirely auspicious; may she, who is the entirety of Fortune (Kamalā), bestow nourishment upon my home, Svāhā!
7.2.16.4 [8.9] He who bears the entirety of all moving beings—may he traverse the whole sky; may a boat be capable [of carrying him] in the water, his form being eternal, svāhā!
7.2.16.5 [8.10] Or he who, from the ten fingers, holds together all those [beings] that are extended, possessing their respective seeds according to the proper time.
For the sake of being beyond sound, for my own strength, for strength, svāhā!

7.2.17.2 [9.2] His breast dwells in the most excellent choice; bearing speech, it has increased everything together.
To that most excellent one, for the increase of boons, svāhā!

7.2.17.3 [9.3] Smaller than the smallest, greater than the greatest, the Self is hidden in the secret place of this living being; through the grace of the Creator, the man whose sorrows have departed beholds Him, the Lord, the majesty, who is beyond volition—svāhā!

7.2.17.4 [9.4] Viṣṇu is the most excellent, the foremost among the givers of boons; he who, meditating upon the universal seers (viśva-ṛṣis), indeed creating the universe, established it as food—unto him, to that Viṣṇu, the sovereign, to the one who bears the immeasurable, Svāhā!
7.2.17.5 [9.5] The lotus-born ones, rejoicing, proclaiming, falling, filling with strength again—that which is the new sprout.
To each and every one of those of equal splendor at their birth, svāhā!

8.1.1.1 That [wheel] has one rim, three folds, sixteen ends, fifty spokes, twenty intermediate spokes, eight sets of six, and a single noose of manifold forms.

may he grant us wealth.

8.1.1.6 Brahmā is the god of gods; in the place of Brahman, I establish this Brahma-jewel. Om! 8.1.2.3 To Agni, I establish this pearl in the place of Agni; *oṃ namaḥ*. 8.1.2.4 Yama has sustained it; to Yama, I establish this lapis lazuli gem in the place of Yama; *oṃ namaḥ*.

8.1.2.5: O Vasus, first ones; O Nirṛtis, I establish this conch-born [conch] in the place of Nirṛti; *oṃ* homage! [*768*] I abandon. 8.1.3.1: O you hundred [powers], for Varuṇa; I establish this crystal gem in the place of Varuṇa; *oṃ* homage!

8.1.3.2 To the Maruts or the Supreme Self, the Winds: I establish this Pushyakanta gem in the place of Vayu; Om, obeisance! 8.1.3.3 To King Soma: I establish this Chandrakanta gem in the place of Soma; Om, obeisance! 8.1.3.4 To Ishana, the Lord of all worlds: I establish this blue gem in the place of Ishana; Om, obeisance!

8.1.3.5 May Vāsuki bestow peace upon us; I establish this amṛta-stone gem in the place of Vāsuki—Oṃ, homage! 8.1.4.1 Dhātṛ, the lord of the world among the sustainers, the divine Savitṛ, the overcomer of adversaries.
May both Aśvins, Bṛhaspati, and the gods protect this sacrifice and the sacrificer from misfortune.

8.1.4.2 To the Sādhyas, I establish this ruby amulet in the station of the Sādhyas; Oṃ, obeisance! 8.1.4.3 To Viśvedeva, to all the gods, I establish this blue-lotus amulet in the station of the Viśvedevas; Oṃ, obeisance!

8.1.4.6 In the abode of the Siddhas, I install this coral gem for the sake of the perfected ones; Om, obeisance!

8.1.4.7. Singing this [hymn] upon my head for the Lord of Life, the senses, the mind, and beloved things—for the sake of the most excellent speech and splendors—may he, establishing a treasure, be for the prosperity of progeny.

One should recite these four [verses] up to the "Gift of Cows" (Ā-go-dāna). This Brāhmī hymn was created by Brahmā; it concerns the Supreme Self. The Self is the undecaying Lord of the immortals among the gods.
Seated upon a full-blown white lotus with a stalk half a palm-tree in length, his eyes red, and resembling a conch or crystal, he was the inner self (*antarātman*) dwelling within those gods.
The unconquered Lord was the inner self of the yakṣas, the vidyādharas, and the gandharvas, as well as the inner self of Brahmā.
That which is brahmic, fierce, and exalted, like the gold of men or pure gold itself— measuring the size of a thumb, seated in the heart, the inner self of all things that stand firm—
is the form entered by Agni; you are its radiance, and he is designated as the living soul (jīva).
